Let me check reference images across these candidates first.

Now I have all 8 reference views. Let me compare:

**Test image**: Single corn leaf with broad, diffuse pale yellow-green bands/stripes running parallel to veins along the full leaf length. Background is soil. Mostly green with large pale yellow-green areas.

**Comparison summary:**
- **Maize_Streak_Virus** (views 1 & 6): Fine dotted/dashed yellow streaks — not matching the broad diffuse bands in test
- **Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus** (views 2 & 5): Narrow light-green striping on young whorl leaves — partially similar but stripes are narrower
- **Stewart_S_Disease** (views 3 & 8): More distinct white/bleached elongated streaks with brownish edges — contrast is sharper than test image
- **Maize_Chlorotic_Dwarf_Virus** (view 4): Broad yellow-green irregular patches along veins (vein banding) — **closest visual match** to test image
- **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma** (view 7): Purple/red discoloration — no match

The test image's broad, diffuse yellow-green banding pattern most closely matches **Maize_Chlorotic_Dwarf_Virus**, which produces vein banding (chlorosis along veins) creating broad pale streaks running the leaf length. The MCDV reference (leaf_42) showed nearly the same pattern: a green leaf with large, diffuse yellow-green patches/bands along the veins.
